newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-HINGIS CLINCHES FOURTH TITLE IN A ROW.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS CLINCHES FOURTH TITLE IN A ROW.

text.p: Swiss teenager Martina Hingis added another win to her impressive start of the season when she clinched her fourth title in as many tournaments in the Paris Open on Sunday.
She bettered her previous record of three titles in a row and launched a strong warning to her German arch-rival Steffi Graf.
On Sunday the 16-year-old top seed, who won the Australian Open last month, overcame strong resistance from the number three seed Anke Huber of Germany to win 6-3 3-6 6-3 in nearly two hours.
"I always have hard times when playing Anke," said the world number two Hingis.
A confident Hingis had made an early break to lead 3-1 before losing her serve in the following game.
But Huber, ranked number seven in the world, appeared nervous while serving and Hingis seized the opportunity to wrap the first set up 6-3 in less than 30 minutes.
The second set swung in the opposite direction as Huber took control to level the score one set all.
In the final set, Huber's erratic serve shortened the game. At 4-3 she double faulted to give Hingis the opportunity to serve for the match.
The Swiss 16-year-old, paired with Czech Jana Novtona, also won the doubles title when they beat Alexandra Fusai of France and Italy's Rita Grande 6-3 6-0.
The Slovak-born Hingis, who is looking forward to a fortnight of rest, will not take part in the Fed Cup tie against her former country in the first days of March.
"I won't play against Slovakia but this is not so important. I am Swiss and I play for Switzerland," she said.
